title: Controls, controllers and Steam Deck - House of Pips Wiki
description: Mouse, keyboard shortcuts, controller support, Steam Input and Steam Deck notes for House of Pips.
html:
Controls, controllers and Steam Deck

You can play House of Pips with a mouse, a keyboard, a controller, or any mix of them. On-screen prompts follow whatever you used last.

Mouse #

  • Click a bone in your rack to pick it up, then click a glowing play location. You can also drag the bone there and let go.
  • Right-click while holding a bone turns it 90 degrees, for the vertical branches of a spinner.
  • Hover almost anything for a tooltip: perks, supplies, bones, scores and buttons.
  • A label or name shortened with dots to fit, as tabs can be at the Extra large text size, shows its full text when you hover it.
  • Buttons have flat backgrounds and colored borders. Hover over an enabled button to show its gold outline.
  • Perks you can use and your table supplies sit left of the table as small buttons showing their icon and remaining uses, each column from the lowest rarity down. Hover one to read its name and what it does. An armed perk wears a gold ring.
  • Click the boneyard when you have no legal play.
  • Click a glowing envelope at the top to inspect a friend's multiplayer invitation. In its panel, Esc or controller Back chooses Later and keeps the invitation. During a table, the controller's action button (Xbox X / PlayStation Square) reaches the envelope with the other table actions.

While holding a bone, Pip Forecast adds compact projected-total numbers beside the landing previews. A small legend in the status column shows what the colors mean: white is the open-end total, pink is a total that scores. Hover the legend for details. An armed placement perk shows its name and remaining uses once in the status column, with a small marker on each affected landing. Hover or focus a landing to inspect its outcome and any required rotation. Loaded End keeps its +1 or −1 cue.

Keyboard #

KeyAction
1 to 0Pick up the bone in that rack slot
Arrow keysCycle through the places the bone can go
EnterPlay the bone at the selected place
RRotate the bone you are holding
EscCancel the current selection
SpaceDraw from the boneyard
LOpen the match ledger
Space or EnterSpeed up draft reveals and hand summaries
Enter or Esc in a confirmationConfirm or cancel it
Arrow keys, Tab, Shift+TabMove between menu buttons
NNext song
F11Toggle fullscreen
F1Toggle menu narration

Controllers #

  • Xbox, PlayStation and Nintendo Switch style controllers and the Steam Deck are supported. Button prompts show the right symbols for your controller.
  • A button prompt that cannot do anything right now is grayed out. While you hold a bone, Place grays out whenever the bone does not fit the end you are aiming at as it is turned.
  • Controls go through Steam Input, so you can remap them in Steam. Open Settings > Access > Edit in Steam. Remapped buttons show their new prompts in the game.
  • Menus, matches and Nana's tutorial all work with a controller.
  • Standalone controller hints have dark bordered panels so their symbols and labels stay readable over the table artwork.
  • By default, PlayStation Cross or Xbox/Steam Deck A confirms the focused choice; Circle or B goes back or cancels. Page arrows use L1/R1 or LB/RB; those buttons switch tabs in the skill tree.
  • Cutscene Pause/Resume uses Triangle/Y. Continue uses Cross/A when its button appears. Rank Up dialogue waits for Continue on each line; Enter also continues it.
  • During the opponent's turn you can inspect your rack. Select dims while the focused bone cannot be played.
  • A committed boneyard draw must finish before you can return to your rack. Rack locked and its Back prompt are dimmed during the choice; choice prompts disappear while the bones slide into your hand.
  • During a committed perk burn and reveal, Cross/A speeds it up. Return to supplies after the result settles.

Steam Deck #

House of Pips plays on Steam Deck, and Steam Cloud carries your career between the Deck and your PC.

  • The game is laid out for the Deck's 1280×800 screen and starts on the Extra large text size there, so small text stays readable. Docked to a 1080p or larger screen it switches to Standard straight away. The Deck's screen and the docked screen each keep the size you choose under Settings > Access > Text size.
  • On the Deck and other screens smaller than 1920×1080, the bones at the open ends, a spinner with an open side included, are drawn larger than the rest of the train, so their pips stay readable however long the train grows. The train makes room for them, so they never cover another bone or a drop target.
  • Large drag targets in Settings make the small screen more comfortable.
